contentBlocks.title: Cancelled — How to Reinstate Your Grant
contentBlocks.description: Your SASSA grant shows 'Cancelled' — don't panic. Learn why grants are cancelled, how to check if it was an error, and the steps to file for reinstatement or submit a new application.

contentBlocks.text: The 'Cancelled' status means your SASSA grant is no longer active. This is a permanent status change, not a temporary hold. Understanding why your grant was cancelled is the first step toward getting it reinstated if you still qualify.
This status affects SASSA grant beneficiaries whose grants have been stopped or terminated by SASSA.

contentBlocks.title: Do Not Ignore Cancellation
contentBlocks.text: Your grant has been stopped. Contact SASSA immediately to understand why your grant was cancelled and whether you can reapply.

contentBlocks.explanation: Your grant has been permanently stopped or archived in the SASSA system. Unlike 'Declined', which applies to a single month, 'Cancelled' means your entire grant registration has been deactivated.
whyItHappens: You voluntarily cancelled your grant (e.g., you found employment)
For child support: the child turned 18 and the grant automatically terminated
You did not collect your grant payments for 3 consecutive months
SASSA detected you qualify for a different grant type
SASSA identified non-compliance with grant conditions
Your grant was transferred to a different grant type
contentBlocks.howLongItLasts: Permanent until you file a formal reinstatement or submit a new application. A cancelled grant does not automatically reactivate.
whatYouShouldDo: If this was a mistake: visit your nearest SASSA office to request reinstatement
If you voluntarily cancelled: no action needed, but you can reapply if circumstances change
If the child turned 18: the child support grant automatically ends, but the child can apply for other grants in their own name if eligible
If you did not collect payments: explain your reason at a SASSA office and request reinstatement

faqs.question: Can I reinstate a cancelled SASSA grant?
faqs.answer: Yes. Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID and explain why your grant was cancelled. You will need to provide current financial documents to prove ongoing eligibility.

faqs.question: How long does reinstatement take?
faqs.answer: Reinstatement processing times vary. In most cases, it takes 2 to 4 weeks for a reinstatement to be processed and payments to resume.

faqs.question: My child's grant was cancelled when they turned 18. Can they still get paid?
faqs.answer: No. The Child Support Grant automatically terminates at age 18. However, if the child is still in secondary school, the grant may be extended to age 21 with a social worker's recommendation.

faqs.question: Can I apply for a new grant if mine was cancelled?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can submit a completely new application at any time if you meet the eligibility criteria.
